output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses comes from the 12 August move of the alert relay server, not from agency staffing. The hardware move silently dropped 11 of 14 forwarding rules. These included the 15-second hold-off for brief SpO2 dips, repeat-notification suppression, and routing of technical alarms to the charge phone. Pods A-C phone notifications per nurse have roughly doubled (about 38 to about 82 per shift). Median acknowledgement time doubled, from 34 s to 71 s. Pod D was still on the old server and shows no change. Incident rates after 12 August are about the same for core, agency and new-graduate nurses (about 4 per 100 shifts), so staff mix does not explain it. The monitor alarm volume was flat, so neither acuity nor the September monitor update explains it. I'm fairly confident (about 85-90%). Do not approve the agency cap or the performance reviews, because they would punish the wrong people. Do not switch off phone forwarding of SpO2 and technical alarms, because that removes a safety net on nights when the central station is unstaffed. Instead, re-import the rules with clinical validation and sign-off, and track phone notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Do the same for Pod D when its phase 2 move happens. Wireless coverage at room 14 is still unchecked. Sick leave may be partly due to alarm load, but that is unproven because the respiratory virus season is a rival explanation.
